The core REST module (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest`) has three resource classes that call `ConceptService.saveDrug` from their write paths. A change to `saveDrug` could affect each of them.

1. **`DrugResource1_8.save`** (`/ws/rest/v1/drug`, the generic drug resource) passes the drug straight to `saveDrug`. It is the main path for drug create and update.
2. **`DrugIngredientResource1_11.save`** adds the ingredient to its parent drug if it is missing, then calls `saveDrug` on that drug (`/drugingredient`).
3. **`DrugIngredientResource1_11.purge`** removes the ingredient from the drug and then calls `saveDrug` to persist the removal.
4. **`DrugReferenceMapResource1_10.save`** attaches the reference map to its drug and calls `saveDrug` (`/drugreferencemap`).

The three `DrugIngredientResource1_11` and `DrugReferenceMapResource1_10` callers are the ones that depend on `saveDrug` persisting the parent drug's child collections, so a change to how `saveDrug` handles ingredients or mappings would hit them hardest. `DrugResource1_8.purge` calls `purgeDrug`, not `saveDrug`, so I left it out.

The `saveDrug` call sites in the test class `DrugController1_10Test` (lines 133 and 144) also exercise this path, but they are tests, so I did not list them as affected code.
